name: ラーメン 霽レ空 (Ramen Haresora)

claims.text: Single small ramen kitchen serving wheat-noodle bowls with shoyu tare; shared boiling water and prep make gluten cross-contact effectively unavoidable.
Bowls are seasoned with a soy-sauce (shoyu) tare, noted as using Maruta soy sauce, which is wheat-containing.
Broths are animal-based (clear pork broth in the current Chinese soba; earlier chicken/oyster), with meat toppings, so no vegan-safe preparation exists.

name: 拉麺 へんてこ (Ramen Henteko)

claims.text: Signature bowls are built on a soy (shoyu) tare; standard Japanese ramen soy tare is wheat-based, and no source indicates otherwise here.
Broth is a long-simmered chicken-bone paitan and bowls carry pork chashu, so the kitchen is animal-based throughout with no vegan preparation noted.

name: ラーメン京都てんぐ 常盤店 (Ramen Kyoto Tengu Tokiwa-ten)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles cooked in a shared boiling pot, plus wheat-wrapped gyoza/shumai/shoronpo on the same line, make gluten cross-contamination unavoidable.
The bowl is a shoyu (soy-sauce) style ramen; Japanese soy sauce almost always contains wheat, so the tare is a wheat source.
Broth is pork-bone and chicken-gara based and finished with pork back fat; chashu pork tops the bowl, so no dish is free of animal products.

name: ラーメン また此処で (Ramen Mata Koko de)

claims.text: Core product is house-made extra-thick wheat noodles boiled in shared pots; gluten is unavoidable and there is no indication of any gluten-free handling.
The tare is a soy-sauce-based (kaeshi) seasoning — standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat — kept light to let the pork-bone broth's sweetness show.
Broth is pork-bone (tonkotsu) with back fat and pork toppings; vegetables are cooked into and mounded over the same animal-based bowl, so no component is free of animal contact.

name: ラーメン 麺対軒 (Ramen Mentaiken)

claims.text: All ramen is built on wheat noodles and a soy-sauce tare, and the kitchen also makes fried rice and Chinese dishes, so shared cookware and gluten exposure throughout are inherent.
The bowls are shoyu (soy-sauce) ramen, including a 'Kyoto black' deep-soy-sauce style; soy-sauce tare for ramen is essentially always wheat-based.
Broth is animal-based dashi with pork chashu; no vegan/vegetable-broth option is indicated.

name: ラーメンムギュ VOL.1本店 (Ramen Mugyu Vol.1 Honten)

claims.text: The broth is described as Nagoya Cochin chicken blended with light soy sauce (薄口醤油); Japanese soy sauce is normally brewed with wheat, making the tare a wheat source on top of the wheat noodles.
The broth is built on Nagoya Cochin chicken and chicken bones and the shop centers on roasted pork belly char siu, so all bowls contain animal products.

name: らーめん セアブラノ神 壬生本店 (Ramen Seabura no Kami Mibu Honten)

claims.text: Bowls use wheat chukamen and a soy-sauce-based tare in a shared ramen kitchen; no gluten-free handling is described.
The signature is described as a combination of dried sardine, pork back fat and soy-sauce soup, indicating a standard wheat-containing shoyu base.
Broth is an ~8-hour chicken-and-pork-bone clear stock finished with pork back fat and dried sardines, so all bowls share animal-based components.

name: ラーメン荘 地球規模で考えろ ソラ (Ramen-so Chikyu Kibo de Kangaero Sora)

claims.text: The broth/tare is a sweet soy-flavored tonkotsu, which in Jiro-style ramen relies on wheat-containing shoyu; combined with the wheat noodles this bowl is not gluten-free.
Pork is fundamental — tonkotsu broth, pork back-fat (アブラ), and char siu — so there is no vegan-safe preparation.
